newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Speculative sell-off hits cocoa.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Speculative sell-off hits cocoa.

text.p: US investment funds baled out of cocoa on Tuesday sending prices down, but in volatile soft commodity markets coffee was firmer in New York and a big retailer put up prices at the check-out.
New York cocoa tumbled some $50 per tonne to $1,397, the lowest level in a month, after waves of speculative selling battered the market and triggered technical sell signals.
In London, sterling-denominated July futures followed suit and slid $42 to $1,002 by the close.

US arabica coffee futures, by contrast, shot higher on Tuesday buoyed by news that Folgers Coffee Co was raising by 20 cents the list price on its standard cans of regular and decaffinated ground coffee.

Industry sources said another rise in retail prices was to be expected after the continuing upswing in coffee futures amid low inventories at roasting plants and the prospect of smaller harvests in many Latin American countries.
"I'm not surprised that Folgers would raise its prices because the market has been so strong," a trader said.
The move could be positive for futures prices near-term because it may encourage consumers to hoard coffee, thereby boosting demand.
London's adequately supplied robusta coffee market ignored the Folgers news, however, and July futures ended $3 lower at $1,597.
In other commodities markets, the precious metals were under pressure with forecasts of further weakness to come, analysts said.
"That seems entirely logical given that we have had a rise in US interest rates, a strengthening dollar and orderly correction on Wall Street," said analyst Andy Smith of Union Bank of Switzerland.
However, benign U.S. economic data which analysts said showed reduced inflationary pressures, had little immediate impact on gold.
Gold closed little changed at $339.95 per ounce, after fixing at an 11-week low of $338.95 in the morning.
"There must be a gravitational pull towards the year low ($336.90) and as that's a four-year low, it opens up a lot of chart territory," Smith added.
The base metals were generally featureless, with flagship copper prices finishing little changed at $2,360 on the London Metal Exchange (LME).
Lead prices, however, fell to an 18-month low and traders said further losses were expected as the winter battery-replacement demand period was over.
Chicago July wheat prices drifted lower to $4.20 per bushel, down $0.75, following better crop weather in the US and France, and a USDA report showed an improvement in the US winter wheat crop.
Concerns about winterkill damage from an April freeze had sent wheat futures higher in recent weeks.
In oil markets benchmark IPE Brent crude futures edged up on unconfirmed talk of problems at a US refinery.
Some key prices at 1745 GMT on Tuesday.
